# Methods

The ADR GIS Atlas is built on a set of reusable analytical workflows for processing administrative, geographic and environmental data.

These methods are shared to improve transparency, reproducibility and collaboration across projects.

## Core Workflows

### Active Postcodes

Identification and cleaning of active postcode records using the ONS Postcode Directory.

Used for:

- Geographic linkage
- Address validation
- Postcode matching

[Active Postcodes](notebooks/active-postcodes.ipynb)
---

### Rural / Urban Classification

Classification of postcodes and locations using official rural and urban definitions.

Used for:

- Population segmentation
- Service accessibility analysis
- Environmental modelling

[Rural Urban Classification](notebooks/rural-urban-classification.ipynb)

---

### Spatial Linkage

Methods for linking postcodes, administrative boundaries and geographic datasets.

Used for:

- Small area statistics
- Nearest-neighbour analysis
- Service catchments

[Spatial Linking](notebooks/spatial-linkage.ipynb)

---

### Identifying locations based on classifications and Open Data

Identifying locations based on open data, using Open Street Map and Companies House data.

Used for:

- Finding places of interest - in this case farms

[Active Postcodes](notebooks/identify-locations.ipynb)

---

### Statistical Pipelines

Reusable workflows for data aggregation, summary statistics and analytical outputs.

Used for:

- Project reporting
- Exploratory analysis
- Data quality checking

[Statistical Pipelines](notebooks/statistical-pipelines.ipynb)

---

### Hex Grid Analysis

Methods for producing location-based summaries using hexagonal grids.

Used for:

- Spatial visualisation
- Coverage analysis
- Density estimation

[Hex Grid Analysis](notebooks/hex-grid-analysis.ipynb)

---

## Reproducibility

Where possible, methods pages include:

- Data sources
- Assumptions
- Processing steps
- Selected code examples
- Links to source notebooks
- Links to GitHub repositories

Code examples are presented in a condensed format to highlight the key analytical steps while keeping pages readable for non-technical collaborators.
